entry.title: Updates for Chrome 159 beta
entry.content:
The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.21.2) found new features shipping in Chromium 159 beta which was released yesterday. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive. Also, if a feature is in Canary/behind flags, it is not considered here. If a feature is missing, one reason can be that the IDL is not yet in a specification or in webref.

Chrome 159 stable releases on December 8, 2026. This PR needs to be merged before/with the BCD release on December 3, 2026.

entry.title: FF161 ClipboardItem web custom formats enabled by default
entry.content:
FF161 enables support for ClipboardItem custom formats (types prefixed with web ) by default on desktop and Android in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2053725

This updates api.ClipboardItem.type_web from preview to 161, and adds notes for the Firefox-specific read restrictions (the spec doesn't restrict reads by origin):

  • Custom formats can only be read if the clipboard contains same-origin content. Firefox treats data from other applications as cross-origin. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2086505
  • Extensions with clipboardRead can read custom formats from any origin. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2087427

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46463

entry.title: FF161 RTCRtpSender.setParameters() setParameterOptions.encodingOptions
entry.content:
FF161 adds support for the setParameterOptions argument of RTCRtpSender.setParameters(), and its encodingOptions property (an array of objects with a keyFrame property), in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2057265

This adds api.RTCRtpSender.setParameters.setParameterOptions_encodingOptions_parameter. keyFrame is the only member of each encodingOptions item, so it doesn't get its own subfeature.

  • Chrome: 122. Added in chromium/chromium@b53076683b (refs/heads/main@{#1249577}), and https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161082937409536 says 122.
  • Safari: false. WebKit's RTCRtpSender.idl still declares only setParameters(RTCRtpSendParameters parameters).

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46464

entry.content:
Summary

Chrome 157 removes most but not all of the Protected Audience API surface.

Some APIs remain, mainly the ProtectedAudience interface itself. I can't confirm its removal just yet (it seems to be in either 159 or 160 but I get inconsistent testing results right now). entry.title: Add extensionTypes.IconVariant and pageAction.setIcon variants, and the Firefox bug for the icon variants APIs.
entry.content:
Summary

Adds extensionTypes.IconVariant and the variants parameter of pageAction.setIcon(), records the any and colorSchemes properties, and adds the Firefox and Chrome bugs for the icon variants APIs.

  • extensionTypes.IconVariant: Safari 18.2. It is a dictionary type, so like ImageDetails it describes the structure the APIs accept, and no browser exposes it on the extensionTypes object.
  • extensionTypes.IconVariant.any and icon_variants.any: Safari 18.2, partial, because Safari prefers any over every explicit size in a group instead of using it only when no other size is large enough: https://webkit.org/b/330501.
  • extensionTypes.IconVariant.colorSchemes: Safari 26.2, with color_schemes as the alternative name from Safari 18.2.
  • icon_variants.color_schemes in the manifest: Safari 18.2.
  • pageAction.setIcon() variants: Safari 18.2. Safari maps pageAction onto the same implementation as action.
  • https://bugzil.la/1955199 is the Firefox impl_url for the type and for the variants and iconVariants parameters of action.setIcon(), browserAction.setIcon(), pageAction.setIcon(), menus.create() and menus.update().
  • https://crbug.com/41419485 is the Chrome impl_url for the type and for action.setIcon().

The mdn_url for the new type is left out until the MDN page exists.

Test results and supporting details

npm run lint -- webextensions passes.

  • mdn/content#46364
  • w3c/webextensions#949

Related issues

Follows #31029 and #31065.
